done_when: forge sync keeps sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access", approval_policy = "never" and [features] hooks = true in .codex/config.toml, and removes top-level model and model_reasoning_effort pins so forge.toml's models and the host's choice govern; every other setting the client has stays as it is, and a file sync can't edit safely refuses as today. A command-level test syncs an old-style config (workspace-write, a model pin, other client settings) and checks the result, and another checks a second sync changes nothing.

findings.body: If a config already has the required sandbox and approval values but contains `[features] hooks = 1`, `data == wanted` is true because Python compares `1 == True` as true. Sync returns without rewriting or refusing the file, leaving `hooks` as a number instead of `true`. The equality check needs a type-sensitive check for `hooks` before returning unchanged.
findings.title: Not done: forge sync keeps sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access", approval_policy = "never" and [features] hooks = true in .codex/config.toml,

why: forge sync only switches Codex hooks on in a client's .codex/config.toml, so Codex sessions in client repos still run sandboxed with approval prompts and can keep a stale model pin from the old Forge, although Forge gives Codex full access
